C0.quote: Truth discovery is a general name for a broad range of statistical methods
C0.note: Paper studies rank aggregation and voting rules for aggregating noisy worker reports into a collective answer.

C1.note: Main formal results are algorithmic/statistical guarantees for the P-TD algorithm; Section 5 reports empirical evaluation on real and synthetic data, e.g. 'We demonstrate on real and synthetic data'.

C2.1.quote: each providing a report in some space Z

C2.2.quote: Any ranking (permutation) L ∈ L(C) corresponds to a binary vector
C2.2.note: RANK for the ranking/rank-aggregation setting; OTH because the general model allows reports in an arbitrary space Z, including binary and real-valued labels.

C2.3.quote: The type ti of a worker determines her distribution of answers
C2.3.note: Workers have types/competence or fault levels defined separately from the submitted report.

C2.4.quote: The type ti of a worker determines her distribution of answers
C2.4.note: The submitted report s_i and the held type t_i are separate objects in the model.

C3.1.quote: Workers each report their answers S, which depend on the ground truth
C3.1.note: Reports follow a noise model, not strategic choice.

C3.2.note: The paper models noisy reports around ground truth, not submission of a held attitude, and does not say voters submit their held attitude.

C4.1.note: Applicability condition not met: the paper evaluates distance/error/accuracy, not voter utility, welfare, satisfaction, cost, distortion, or intensity of preference.

C4.2.note: The term 'dichotomous preferences' is not used.

C5.1.quote: The error of every algorithm is the distance ... to the ground truth
C5.1.note: Results are evaluated by accuracy/error relative to ground truth, not by welfare, efficiency, satisfaction, representation, proportionality, or distortion.

VOT.quote_behav: Workers each report their answers S, which depend on the ground truth
VOT.note: Workers' reports are generated by an exogenous noise model; information assumptions are not applicable for NONSTRAT behaviour.

CAN.note: Candidates are alternatives in rankings, not agents taking actions.

ORG.note: No organizer/chair or election authority chooses actions in the formal model.

DES.note: Rule design is not modeled as an explicit designer choice.

C7.1.note: Only voters are present as agents.

C8.1.note: No strategic or mixed types, so solution concepts do not apply.

claims.quote: results in substantial improvement over unweighted aggregation and other truth discovery algorithms
the P-TD algorithm substantially improves the outcome compared to unweighted aggregation
average similarity heuristic is indeed a frustratingly easy—and practical—tool for crowdsourcing

C9.1.note: Abstract and conclusion make claims about practical improvement and the usefulness of the method.

C9.2.quote: We do not make any assumptions regarding the ground truth z
C9.2.note: The formal modelling assumptions behind the claims, such as the noise model and type-dependent report distribution, are stated. Empirical performance claims are directly based on the described datasets and evaluation.

C10.1.note: The paper relates reports to underlying ground truth and noise rather than taking a purely procedural, input-only reading.
